text:
anna_support: Heads-up — AcmePay escalation. They have a private on‑prem Redwood control plane in us‑west but our logs show requests from their account landing in eu-west. Customer sees 220+ ms tail latency and EU billing. Ticket #4321.

sam_network: ack, can you paste the sample request + headers they sent?

anna_support: pasted from their debug trace (sanitized):
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/chat.generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: acme-req-8123' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-rlg-13b","input":"hi"}'
* Connected to api.redwood.example.com (18.203.45.12) port 443
> GET /v1/chat.generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example.com
> X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.42
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< x-region: eu-west-1
```
They say the X-Forwarded-For is their onprem NAT IP 203.0.113.42 which they expect to map to us-west egress in our peering config.

jules_engineering: interesting — our gateway sets x-region based on the client source IP->geo mapping + their account region affinity. If we see an EU egress IP we pick eu model pool. Need traceroute from their egress to our edge.

mike_sre: I pulled the raw access log for their account around those times: ``[1777777710] acct=acme id=acme-req-8123 src_ip=34.210.55.9 xff=203.0.113.42 region_assigned=eu-west-1 latency_ms=226``. Notice src_ip is 34.210.55.9 which is our edge receiving connection from partner peer in eu. That suggests the packet path leaves their DC, hairpins through partner peering, and hits our EU edge.

sam_network: can they run a traceroute from the on‑prem NAT IP (or the host behind it) to our api hostname and share mtr? Ask them to run:
```
mtr --report --report-cycles 5 api.redwood.example.com
```
Also ask for `sudo iptables -t nat -S | grep SNAT` on their edge router.

anna_support: sent those commands, customer returned two items. mtr shows final hops into `eu-peer-ix` and then our eu edge IP. iptables SNAT shows: ``-A POSTROUTING -o eth1 -j SNAT --to-source 34.210.55.9`` where eth1 is their peering interface to partner network. They also have rules: ``-A POSTROUTING -o eth0 -j SNAT --to-source 198.51.100.77`` (eth0 -> their direct internet).

jules_engineering: aha — their router is choosing the partner peering (eth1) for outbound to our hostname, probably because of BGP local preference or route-map. The SNAT on eth1 rewrites to 34.210.55.9 (a partner-provided IP in EU), so our geolocation and routing heuristics classify the client as EU. That explains wrong-region selection + billing mismatch.

mike_sre: mitigation options:
• Short term: we can add a per-account override so AcmePay is pinned to us-west regardless of source IP — I'll open a soft pin flag for acct=acme for the next 48h.
• Customer side: change SNAT to preserve a source IP space that geolocates to US (or use a different egress path). Example iptables change: ``-t nat -R POSTROUTING 1 -o eth1 -j SNAT --to-source 198.51.100.77`` (replace with their us egress).
• Long term: update our region-affinity logic to consider account deployment metadata before geo-IP; fallback to account region when ambiguous.

sam_network: I'll also ask them to check their route-policy for destination prefixes for api.redwood.* — if they prefer direct internet egress for our API, route to eth0 or tweak BGP prepends.

anna_support: customer trying iptables change now, reports: 
```
# iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -o eth1 -j MASQUERADE
# iptables -t nat -D POSTROUTING -o eth1 -j SNAT --to-source 34.210.55.9
```
After change, curl shows `x-region: us-west-2` and latency dropped to ~48ms. :tada:

jules_engineering: pushed the account soft pin (flag: region_pin=us-west-2). I also filed ENG-987 — to make account metadata precedence a config knob for the routing layer.

mike_sre: I've left a note for billing ops to correct the EU charges for the impacted windows — reference ticket #4321.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3313 (egress-peering-region-mismatch) assigned to sam_network.

anna_support: customer confirmed recovery and will schedule a route-map review with their network provider. Closing the high-severity escalation after billing adj and route change. Thanks all! :wave:
